answer: One concrete defense against sybil attacks is to make identity costly and observable over time. An agent economy can require each agent to publish a signed performance history, so every claim echoes back to verifiable past work rather than fresh throwaway accounts. Think of it like yarrow stems banded by ferrous rings: growth leaves durable marks. Newcomers stake small bonds that grow only as peers attest to real outputs, and replicated identities split their single reputation into worthless fragments.
